title: Claude 20x is now Ultra without the 5-hour limit
content:
This article explains what the Ultra plan includes, how much it costs, and how its usage limits work.
This article is about paid Ultra plans for individual consumers. If you're part of an organization looking to use Claude with your team, refer to Team and Enterprise plans.
Key benefits
- More usage capacity: Get 10 times the Pro plan's usage every week.
- No five-hour limit for verified accounts: Work at your own pace within your weekly limit. For more information, see What is a verified account?
- Priority access: Be among the first to experience new models, features, and products.
- Access to Claude Code: Use Claude Code for your terminal-based coding workflows with one unified subscription.
- Longer, multi-step tasks: Hand Claude work like reports, spreadsheets, and presentations, and it keeps going in the background. Learn more in Claude Cowork and chat are one Claude.
- Monthly API credits: Ultra plans include monthly credits for the Claude API. Learn more about monthly API credits for Max, Ultra, and Team plans.
What changed from Max 20x?
The Max 20x plan is now called the Ultra plan. Existing Max 20x subscribers move to Ultra automatically, with no price change.
Ultra includes 10 times the Pro plan’s usage every week and has no five-hour limit, for verified accounts.
How much does the Ultra plan cost?
The Ultra plan is available for $200 per month.
Note: This price is for web subscriptions only. Mobile pricing may vary depending on your app platform.
Price and plans are subject to change at Anthropic's discretion.
Billing information
- The Ultra plan is currently available as a monthly subscription only.
- When moving from an annual Pro plan to an Ultra plan, if the remaining balance on your annual Pro plan is greater than your Ultra plan price, you will receive a credit to your account for the remaining balance. This credit will be applied to future subscription costs. 
  - To receive your credit, the billing address used to purchase your Ultra plan must be the same as your previous subscription’s billing address.
  - If your billing address has changed, you will need to cancel your Pro subscription and wait for the subscription end date before signing up for a new Ultra subscription with a new billing address.
  - If you subscribed through Google Play, you're charged the full price of your new plan when you upgrade. The unused value of your previous plan is converted into extra days on your new plan, so your renewal date will land a few days later than a full month.
Does the Ultra plan have any usage limits?
Yes. The Ultra plan includes 10 times the Pro plan's usage every week.
Verified Ultra accounts don't have a five-hour limit. If your account isn't verified yet, a temporary limit applies. For more information, see What is a verified account?
Ultra plans have a weekly usage limit that applies across all models, and a separate weekly limit for Fable.
Additional usage limits may apply to manage capacity and ensure fair access to all users. For example, we may limit your usage in other ways, such as weekly and monthly caps or model and feature usage, at our discretion. We don't guarantee uninterrupted service.
Learn more about usage and length limits and usage limit best practices.
Note: If you have a limit reset, you can use it to reset your weekly usage limits back to full. Learn more about limit resets.
What is a verified Ultra account?
To help prevent fraud and abuse, we automatically verify Ultra accounts using factors like your account and payment history. Verified accounts don't have a five-hour limit.
If your account isn't verified yet, a temporary limit applies. We remove it automatically once your account is verified, so there's nothing you need to do. Verifying your phone number at checkout is a separate step and doesn't remove this limit.
To check, go to Settings > Usage. If you don't see a Current session bar, your account is verified.

report.summary: Anthropic renames its $200/month Max 20x plan to Ultra, dropping the five-hour session cap for verified users and bundling Claude Code plus API credits.
report.background: Anthropic's consumer lineup has settled into a three-tier ladder: a free tier, Pro at roughly $20/month, and a $200/month power-user tier that launched as Max 5x and Max 20x alongside the rise of agentic coding tools. The binding constraint for heavy users has never been model quality but metering. Professional and semi-professional developers run Claude Code sessions that execute shell commands, edit repositories and iterate for hours, which collides directly with five-hour rolling session windows and weekly caps. Competing offerings — notably OpenAI's $200 ChatGPT Pro tier and various coding-agent subscriptions — have made the flat-fee, high-usage plan a standard product category. At the same time, account sharing and resale of high-quota subscriptions have pushed vendors toward light identity verification. Anthropic's rename reframes the top plan around continuous work rather than raw multiplier language, and the included API credits signal an intent to keep heavy developers inside one subscription instead of splitting spend between a chat plan and metered API billing.
key_points: Same price, new name: Max 20x is now the Ultra plan at $200 per month, and existing Max 20x subscribers were migrated automatically with no price change. It is currently monthly-only, and the price covers web subscriptions, with mobile app store pricing varying by platform.

The session cap is gone: Ultra gives 10 times the Pro plan's weekly usage, and verified accounts no longer hit a five-hour session limit. Effectively, users can spend their weekly allowance at whatever pace they like, which matters most for long agent runs rather than short bursts.

Verification is the catch: Anthropic automatically verifies Ultra accounts using signals such as account age and payment history to curb fraud and abuse. Unverified accounts keep a temporary limit until review completes, and separately verifying a phone number at checkout does not remove it.

More than chat capacity: Ultra bundles Claude Code into the same subscription, priority access to new models and features, monthly Claude API credits, and background execution of multi-step work like reports, spreadsheets and presentations that you can hand off and leave running.

Fine print remains: a separate weekly limit applies to something called Fable, additional weekly and monthly caps or feature limits may be imposed at Anthropic's discretion for capacity management, and uninterrupted service is explicitly not guaranteed.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the move confirms the $200/month flat-fee power tier as a durable category and shifts the competitive battleground from session windows to weekly quotas — a friendlier meter for autonomous agents. Bundling API credits into a consumer subscription blurs the line between seat-based and usage-based pricing, pressuring rivals to do the same. For developers, removal of the five-hour cap is the substantive change: long refactors, test-fix loops and overnight background jobs no longer need to be chopped around reset timers, and one subscription now covers terminal agent work plus API experimentation. For regular users, little changes day to day — Pro remains the entry point — but heavier aggregate consumption by Ultra users could tighten capacity for everyone, and the discretionary-caps language leaves room for future throttling.
report.tools: Worth watching: Claude Code for terminal-based agent workflows, now included with Ultra, and the Claude API credits that let you prototype against models directly. Open-source projects like Cline and Aider offer comparable agentic coding loops and are useful for benchmarking whether a $200 plan pays off. Usage-tracking utilities such as ccusage help monitor Claude Code token spend against weekly quotas, and the built-in limit-reset feature is worth understanding before you commit to a month.
